findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method of that name introduced by this diff is the one-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) declared in the subclass UsernamePasswordForm (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162); no no-arg method is defined in UsernameForm, its superclass AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or anywhere else in this diff, so the reference cannot be resolved. The services module fails to compile with 'cannot find symbol: method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()' because Java resolves the unqualified no-arg call against UsernameForm/AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator and a one-arg overload in a subclass is not visible from the superclass, breaking the entire build; additionally, the new PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication test requires this predicate to return true when passkeys are enabled (otherwise UsernameForm still skips the form via context.success() and re-authentication completes without any credential check), which no definition in the diff supplies.

[BUG] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) requires user != null, and both call sites gate webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on it (authenticate() at line 115 and challenge(String,String) at ~line 137), inverting the pre-image gating which set up the WebAuthn/passkeys form data exactly when no user was selected (the removed code sat inside the context.getUser() == null block, and the removed challenge() check was context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()). On every initial login with passkeys enabled, UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() runs with context.getUser() == null, isConditionalPasskeysEnabled returns false, fillContextForm is never invoked, and the login page is rendered without the embedded form[@id='webauth'] and without the 'username webauthn' conditional-UI autocomplete, so fresh-login passkey authentication stops working entirely; the diff's own tests fail on this: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey asserts loginPage.getUsernameAutocomplete() is 'username webauthn' and that form[@id='webauth'] exists right after a fresh oauth.openLoginForm() following logout(), and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey's unchanged first-page assertion requires form[@id='webauth'] to be present before any user is identified.

[BUG] The new test webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication contains no re-authentication step: its body is a verbatim copy of the first-login passwordLoginWithExternalKey flow (registerDefaultUser, logout, oauth.openLoginForm, webAuthnLoginPage.clickAuthenticate, expectLogin, logout) and never opens the login form with OIDCLoginProtocol.PROMPT_VALUE_LOGIN or performs any second authentication, despite the test name and its comment ('Test users is able to authenticate with passkey during re-authentication') claiming re-authentication coverage. Maintainers reading the test name will believe passkey re-authentication with an external (non-discoverable) key is covered by this test; it actually only re-tests first login, so the scenario's real coverage lives solely in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey — pruning or weakening that 'redundant' sibling later silently drops the coverage while this misnamed test keeps passing green.

[ADVISORY] UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field) no longer sets up passkey conditional UI when no user is resolved: the pre-PR guard explicitly matched context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), and its replacement isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) hard-returns false for a null user, so any error challenge rendered before a user is resolved (e.g., submitting the login form with a missing username during first login) re-renders the login page without the passkey section the pre-PR code added. On passkeys-enabled realms the initial login page offers passkey autofill but the error page shown after a submit that fails before user resolution does not — a first-factor UX inconsistency regressed relative to pre-PR behavior, and the 'conditional UI is offered on every username/password render when passkeys are enabled' invariant is now enforced nowhere for the user==null case in this class.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff exercises the newly added AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call inside WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse — the failed-passkey-during-re-authentication path; the new re-auth tests cover only the failed-password path (badPasswordHandler) and successful passkey re-authentication, and no pre-existing test can cover this path because re-authentication with passkeys was broken before this PR. A regression in this new wiring (the call being dropped in a refactor, or the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note not being set/read at that point) ships green, and users whose passkey attempt fails during re-authentication are shown a fresh-login-style form with the username field and registration link visible instead of the re-auth form the PR establishes.

[ADVISORY] The fix expands passkey conditional UI to every username-password render where a user is resolved, not only re-authentication: the org-flow test's expectation for normal first-factor login was flipped from 'webauthn form absent' (Assert.assertThrows NoSuchElementException) to 'webauthn form present' on the password page, both before and after the failed-password attempt (second flip at the 'correct login now' block), shipping a user-visible change to ordinary login inside a PR titled as a re-authentication fix. Users with non-discoverable passkeys on passkeys-enabled realms now get a webauthn section on the password page during every ordinary login where conditional-UI autofill cannot offer their credential type — a product-behavior change to the normal login flow that is invisible in the PR title and only discoverable through the flipped test assertions, so it should be explicitly confirmed as intended product behavior rather than an incidental side effect of the re-auth mechanism.

[BUG] The WebAuthn fill condition in challenge(error, field) was inverted: it changed from `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, whose added method requires `user != null`, so error challenges rendered while no user is resolved no longer receive any WebAuthn form data. First-factor error pages rendered through this challenge — submitting an unknown username on the username/password form, or username validation failures routed from action() — previously got fillContextForm (the old condition fired exactly on user==null renders) and showed the hidden webauth form plus the passkey conditional-UI autocomplete; after this change those same renders get no WebAuthn data, so a passkey user who mistypes the username loses the one-gesture passkey option on the error page and must reload to get it back. No test in this diff covers a user==null error render (the new error-page test, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, only exercises the user!=null re-auth case).

[ADVISORY] Passkeys-availability gating is now encoded in same-named predicates with different signatures and divergent semantics: the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` here folds in `user != null`, while UsernameForm's pre-existing no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (called at UsernameForm.java:47) cannot check the user, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled()` is a third variant — the single question 'when is passkey conditional UI set up' is now answered by three near-identically named checks. The next passkeys change (new policy flag, per-user credential check, new render path) must locate and keep all of these predicates in sync; the diff itself already demonstrates the drift (user!=null in one, absent in the other), and an edit that assumes they are interchangeable — e.g. copying this re-auth gate into UsernameForm's skip condition or vice versa — silently changes when the form is skipped or filled for first-factor vs re-authentication, with no compiler help because the arity differs.

[ADVISORY] The re-authentication skip is now gated solely on a realm/feature-level check (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` takes no user argument), so in any realm with passkeys enabled the username form is shown on every prompt=login re-authentication, including for users who possess no passkey credential at all. Password-only users hitting flows that contain the username-form execution get an extra username-entry page during re-authentication that did not exist before this change (previously the form was skipped and re-auth went straight to the password page with the username hidden); the decision point has the UserModel in scope and could consult the user's actual passwordless credentials, but the gate as written is realm-policy-level only, so the cost is paid by every re-authenticating user, not just passkey users.

[BUG] authenticate() now gates the WebAuthn conditional-UI setup on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), and the newly added helper requires user != null, which inverts the previous gating ('setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected'), so the initial page of a fresh (unidentified) login no longer receives the passkey conditional-UI form. In a passkey-enabled realm every fresh login renders the username/password page without form#webauth and without autocomplete='username webauthn', making passkeys unusable for normal login; the assertions preserved in this very diff (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey after logout(), and the unchanged first-page webauthn-form assertion in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) now fail, so the refactor silently traded the primary passkeys login flow for the re-authentication fix.

[BUG] challenge(context, error, field) replaced the removed condition context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (which requires user != null) — the exact inverse — so the WebAuthn form data is no longer set up when the page is re-rendered after a failed attempt by a not-yet-identified user. After a failed fresh login (e.g. wrong password) the error page no longer offers the passkey option the removed code deliberately provided for the unidentified-user case, so a user who mistypes the password loses the passkey fallback until the authentication flow is restarted; no test in the diff covers this fresh-login error path.

[ADVISORY] The re-authentication shortcut in UsernameForm.authenticate is now bypassed whenever realm-level passkeys are enabled, because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() checks only the realm policy and does not consider whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey. In realms with passkeys enabled, every re-authentication (prompt=login / step-up) through a UsernameForm-based flow now shows an extra username form even to password-only users who cannot use passkeys, a UX regression for the majority of users that no test in this diff covers (the new re-auth tests only exercise users that own a passkey).

[ADVISORY] The newly added AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call in createErrorResponse is never executed by any test change in this diff: no test triggers a failed passkey ceremony during re-authentication (the only failures simulated anywhere in the three changed test files are wrong-password logins, which route through UsernamePasswordForm.challenge, not the conditional-UI error path). A regression in the passkey-failure-during-re-auth error path (e.g., the error page rendering with the username field visible and registration enabled, allowing identity switch mid-re-authentication) ships with zero test coverage; checked PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java — the only test files in the diff — and none exercises this branch.

[ADVISORY] The shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() override returning false has no asserting test: its only behavioral effect (suppressing the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean list during re-authentication, where the inherited default user != null would return true) is never distinguished, because every test in the diff asserts only form[@id='webauth'] presence, which holds whether or not the authenticator list is rendered. A future change flipping this override back to the default would render the user's authenticator names on the re-authentication page — the disclosure the override's comment says it exists to prevent — with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The negative assertion wraps driver.findElement in catch (Exception) instead of asserting NoSuchElementException, so any lookup exception (e.g., a WebDriverException from a page transition or stale browser state) is treated as 'expected' and the test passes without the webauthn form's absence ever being verified. CI can pass on a broken page state where 'webauthn button not shown' was never actually checked; the precise idiom (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)) used elsewhere in this same test family is strictly stronger at identical cost.

[ADVISORY] The same over-broad catch (Exception) pattern is repeated for the re-authentication-page check, so the 'webauthn button absent during re-auth' assertion passes on any exception rather than specifically on element absence. Same as the first site: a flaky or broken page state during the prompt=login re-auth step is silently accepted as the expected 'no webauthn button' outcome, masking real rendering problems in the newly changed challenge() path.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff covers re-authentication with passkeys ENABLED for a user who has NO passkey credential: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), leaving the isPasskeysEnabled()==true × no-passkey-credential combination — exactly the population whose username-form skip behavior the changed condition in UsernameForm.authenticate (user != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) now governs differently — untested. A regression specific to password-only users re-authenticating in passkeys-enabled realms (e.g., the newly shown username form breaking the flow, or conditional UI being set up for a user with no discoverable credentials) ships untested; checked PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java — every re-auth test in the diff uses a user that possesses a passkey, and the only no-passkey test turns the feature off entirely.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a behavior change in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)`: the pre-change guard explicitly executed `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. After the change, it only fills when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and that method returns false when `user == null` (`... && user != null`). Therefore, on error challenges rendered before a user is resolved (e.g., missing/invalid username on first-factor), the form will no longer have the WebAuthn conditional UI context that previously would have been set up. The same regression exists in `authenticate()` where the initial render also now requires a non-null user to call `fillContextForm`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` inside `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` (to keep the re-authentication form state when a passkey attempt fails). The new/modified tests in this diff focus on (a) successful passkey login during re-authentication (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), and (b) failed-password handling during re-authentication (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` checks an invalid password error and that the webauthn form remains). None of the added tests appear to force a *failed WebAuthn/passkey* attempt that would execute `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`, so the newly introduced wiring could regress without a failing test. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect in the code shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change when passkey/conditional-UI WebAuthn data is filled/shown in UsernamePasswordForm: both authenticate() and challenge(error,field) switch from `context.getUser() == null && passkeysEnabled` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (i.e., passkeys enabled AND user != null). That expands WebAuthn form setup to cases where the user is already resolved (ordinary username->password step, org flow, etc.), not just the prior “user not already selected” behavior. Correspondingly, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest flips assertions from “webauthn form absent” to “present” on the password page after username selection (before/after failed password). This is a real, diff-grounded product/UX behavior change that should be explicitly confirmed as intended scope rather than an incidental side effect of the re-authentication fix, but it is not provably a correctness bug from the diff alone.

This is a verifiable behavioral change: any error challenge rendered while `context.getUser()` is still null will no longer get WebAuthn/passkeys form context populated. The diff also does not add a test that exercises a `user == null` error-render path (the added tests focus on re-authentication where the user is already known).

Even if this is not a functional defect by itself, it creates a concrete maintainability/consistency risk shown by the diff: the user-null condition is encoded in one place but not necessarily in the other, and the overlapping naming makes it easy to apply the wrong predicate when modifying first-factor vs re-authentication behavior.

Password-only users hitting flows that contain the username-form execution get an extra username-entry page during re-authentication that did not exist before this change (previously the form was skipped and re-auth went straight to the password page with the username hidden); the decision point has the UserModel in scope and could consult the user's actual passwordless credentials, but the gate as written is realm-policy-level only, so the cost is paid by every re-authenticating user, not just passkey users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show UsernameForm’s re-authentication skip condition changing to `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no user argument), which could affect when the username form is skipped. However, the finding’s core claim—that `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is “solely a realm/feature-level check” and therefore forces the username form to be shown for *all* re-auth users in passkeys-enabled realms (including password-only users)—cannot be verified from this diff because the implementation of `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is not shown/changed here. The diff does add a *different* helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm (which explicitly requires `user != null`), but that does not establish the semantics of the no-arg method used by UsernameForm.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] authenticate() now gates the WebAuthn conditional-UI setup on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), and the newly added helper requires user != null, which inverts the previous gating ('setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected'), so the initial page of a fresh (unidentified) login no longer receives the passkey conditional-UI form. In a passkey-enabled realm every fresh login renders the username/password page without form#webauth and without autocomplete='username webauthn', making passkeys unusable for normal login; the assertions preserved in this very diff (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey after logout(), and the unchanged first-page webauthn-form assertion in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) now fail, so the refactor silently traded the primary passkeys login flow for the re-authentication fix.

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() the call to webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) was moved out and is now gated by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), and the helper explicitly requires user != null. Previously, fillContextForm was executed when passkeys were enabled even in the branch where the user was not already selected (fresh login with context.getUser() == null). The same new gating is applied in challenge(). From this diff alone, there is no longer any UsernamePasswordForm-side path that populates the conditional-UI/passkeys form data for an unidentified user, which risks removing form#webauth / username-webAuthn autocomplete on the initial login page. The tests in this diff still assert the webauthn form exists immediately after openLoginForm() (e.g., PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest), making the regression directly diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] challenge(context, error, field) replaced the removed condition context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (which requires user != null) — the exact inverse — so the WebAuthn form data is no longer set up when the page is re-rendered after a failed attempt by a not-yet-identified user. After a failed fresh login (e.g. wrong password) the error page no longer offers the passkey option the removed code deliberately provided for the unidentified-user case, so a user who mistypes the password loses the passkey fallback until the authentication flow is restarted; no test in the diff covers this fresh-login error path.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)`, the old condition explicitly handled the *unidentified user* case (`context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) by calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. The diff replaces it with `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, whose implementation requires `user != null`, so the fill call can no longer happen when `context.getUser()` is null. This is an observable behavioral change: when the user isn’t resolved (e.g., fresh login error paths where no `UserModel` is set), the WebAuthn/passkeys form attributes will no longer be populated on re-render, removing the passkey fallback that the removed code path supported. The added/updated tests exercise re-authentication and identified-user scenarios, but do not cover the “user == null on error re-render” path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The re-authentication shortcut in UsernameForm.authenticate is now bypassed whenever realm-level passkeys are enabled, because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() checks only the realm policy and does not consider whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey. In realms with passkeys enabled, every re-authentication (prompt=login / step-up) through a UsernameForm-based flow now shows an extra username form even to password-only users who cannot use passkeys, a UX regression for the majority of users that no test in this diff covers (the new re-auth tests only exercise users that own a passkey).

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes UsernameForm.authenticate to skip the re-authentication shortcut only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (previously it skipped whenever `context.getUser() != null`). This means that in any flow using `UsernameForm`, a re-authentication user will now be forced through the username step whenever conditional passkeys are considered enabled, regardless of whether the specific user can actually use passkeys (no user-credential check is shown here). The added/updated tests in this diff focus on `UsernamePasswordForm`-based flows (e.g., `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`) and do not cover the `UsernameForm` re-authentication shortcut behavior, so the potential UX regression for password-only users in `UsernameForm` flows is not exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The newly added AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call in createErrorResponse is never executed by any test change in this diff: no test triggers a failed passkey ceremony during re-authentication (the only failures simulated anywhere in the three changed test files are wrong-password logins, which route through UsernamePasswordForm.challenge, not the conditional-UI error path). A regression in the passkey-failure-during-re-auth error path (e.g., the error page rendering with the username field visible and registration enabled, allowing identity switch mid-re-authentication) ships with zero test coverage; checked PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java — the only test files in the diff — and none exercises this branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` by calling `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);`, which only affects the UI when a *passkey/conditional UI* ceremony fails during re-authentication. The only newly/modified tests in the diff (in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`, `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`) exercise successful passkey re-authentication and wrong-password failures routed through `UsernamePasswordForm` (e.g., assertions on "Invalid password."), but none appears to intentionally trigger a failing WebAuthn/passkey ceremony that would execute `createErrorResponse()` and validate the username-hidden/registration-disabled attributes. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap rather than a functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() override returning false has no asserting test: its only behavioral effect (suppressing the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean list during re-authentication, where the inherited default user != null would return true) is never distinguished, because every test in the diff asserts only form[@id='webauth'] presence, which holds whether or not the authenticator list is rendered. A future change flipping this override back to the default would render the user's authenticator names on the re-authentication page — the disclosure the override's comment says it exists to prevent — with no failing test.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a new hook `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (default `context.getUser() != null`) and changes `fillContextForm()` to rely on it. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides this to `return false` with a comment that authenticators should not be shown during conditional passkeys login. However, the added/updated tests in the diff only assert presence/absence of the WebAuthn form (`//form[@id='webauth']`) and general flow outcomes; they do not assert that the authenticator list (from `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean`) is suppressed when `context.getUser() != null` during re-authentication. So a regression flipping the override back to default would not necessarily fail these tests, making this a concrete missing-coverage issue for newly introduced behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The negative assertion wraps driver.findElement in catch (Exception) instead of asserting NoSuchElementException, so any lookup exception (e.g., a WebDriverException from a page transition or stale browser state) is treated as 'expected' and the test passes without the webauthn form's absence ever being verified. CI can pass on a broken page state where 'webauthn button not shown' was never actually checked; the precise idiom (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)) used elsewhere in this same test family is strictly stronger at identical cost.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the diff adds negative checks for the webauthn form using `try { driver.findElement(...); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }` (done twice). Catching broad `Exception` can mask unrelated Selenium/WebDriver failures (stale element, navigation timing, driver errors), allowing the test to pass without actually verifying absence. The finding matches the diff and suggests a stronger, already-used pattern (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`) seen elsewhere in this test suite (e.g., other passkeys tests in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same over-broad catch (Exception) pattern is repeated for the re-authentication-page check, so the 'webauthn button absent during re-auth' assertion passes on any exception rather than specifically on element absence. Same as the first site: a flaky or broken page state during the prompt=login re-auth step is silently accepted as the expected 'no webauthn button' outcome, masking real rendering problems in the newly changed challenge() path.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the diff adds two blocks that assert the WebAuthn button is absent using `try { driver.findElement(...); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. This catches any Exception (not just NoSuchElementException) and even includes a meaningless `assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue())` (findElement never returns null), so a broken/flaky page state during the new prompt=login re-auth step could be silently accepted as “button absent”, masking real UI/rendering failures. This is a test robustness issue, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test in the diff covers re-authentication with passkeys ENABLED for a user who has NO passkey credential: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), leaving the isPasskeysEnabled()==true × no-passkey-credential combination — exactly the population whose username-form skip behavior the changed condition in UsernameForm.authenticate (user != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) now governs differently — untested. A regression specific to password-only users re-authenticating in passkeys-enabled realms (e.g., the newly shown username form breaking the flow, or conditional UI being set up for a user with no discoverable credentials) ships untested; checked PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java — every re-auth test in the diff uses a user that possesses a passkey, and the only no-passkey test turns the feature off entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes re-authentication behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate` from skipping the username form whenever `context.getUser() != null` to skipping only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. That introduces/changes a nontrivial branch specifically when a user is already set (reauth) and conditional passkeys are enabled. In the added/modified tests, all re-authentication scenarios exercise users who do have passkey credentials, and the only “no passkey” re-auth test (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`) turns passkeys off realm-wide (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`), so it does not cover the combination “passkeys enabled in realm/profile” + “user has no passkey credential” that the new condition may affect. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven defect.
